description: I participated alone in the creation of Critterlift.
summary: CritterLift helps people who find injured wildlife get the animal to help fast. You snap a photo, the app triages the animal and the urgency, and it routes the case to the nearest rehabber or rescue. It also uses NASA active fire and heat data to warn when wildfires or extreme heat put animals in an area at risk, so rescues can get ahead of a surge.
details:
When I was 22, my friend hit a raccoon with his car. We pulled over and wanted to help, but we had no idea what to do, who to call, or whether it was safe to touch. While we searched for answers, the raccoon died. That night stuck with me, and it's why I built CritterLift.

What it does: CritterLift is a web app that turns a panicked moment into clear steps. You snap a photo of the injured animal, get a triage result that tells you how urgent it is and what to do right now, and get connected to the nearest wildlife rescue or rehabber. It also uses NASA FIRMS active fire data (MODIS and VIIRS) to flag areas where wildfires and extreme heat are injuring and displacing wildlife, so finders and rescues know where help is needed most.

Benefits and impact: Most people who find a hurt animal want to help but freeze, like we did. CritterLift gives everyday people the confidence to act in the first few minutes, when it matters most, and helps rescues see surges coming during fire and heat events. My intention is for this to become a real, usable tool for animal welfare, not just a hackathon demo.

Tools: Built as a web app deployed on Vercel (critterlift.vercel.app), using AI-assisted photo triage, SerpApi for live search results, and NASA FIRMS fire data.

Creativity and factors we considered: CritterLift connects satellite fire data to something personal: one animal on the side of the road. We designed it for stressed people on their phones, so it's fast, simple, and needs no install. We also considered safety, telling users when not to handle an animal and when to wait for a professional.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) active fire data, MODIS and VIIRS
